rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE, so there is headroom to raise obfuscation intensity across the board. The program is tiny (217 lines, 34 functions, ~3.6KB text) and is a C++ tree-manipulation benchmark dominated by short methods plus a moderately sized main, so size overhead is not a real constraint and I raised SecurityGain/DiversityGain for all passes, most aggressively for BCF (bogus control flow is the strongest static-analysis deterrent on branchy tree code) and FLA (flattening main and the Tree constructors destroys the already-small CFGs). SUB stays high on security with low risk since arithmetic substitution is safe on this code. SPLIT, IBR, ICALL, and IGV keep moderate-but-raised security weights because their combined structural noise (block splitting, indirect branches, indirect calls, global variable indirection) compounds diversity cheaply, and all retain low CorrectnessRisk values since round 0 showed the pipeline is stable here. RuntimeCost weights are kept in the 0.3-0.55 band rather than maxed: the runtime dimension still matters for acceptable performance, so heavier passes (BCF, FLA) are moderately penalized while cheap structural passes (SPLIT, IBR, IGV) face little penalty, letting the selector favor low-cost obfuscation on hot small functions and heavy obfuscation on larger ones like main.
